the azygos fissure as a curvilinear line in the right upper lung zone.", "Locate the expected position of the azygos vein (teardrop opacity) at the inferior aspect of the fissure.", "Determine if the opacity is absent from its usual location within the fissure.", "Assess for signs of mediastinal shift or lung re-expansion that could displace mediastinal structures.", "Conclude that absence of the opacity within the fissure, in this context, indicates medial displacement of the azygos vein out of the fissure rather than resolution of fluid or collapse of the vein."]}, {"category": "reasoning", "trigger": "When evaluating a lung opacity that appears to respect anatomical boundaries (fissures) on chest X-ray to determine the underlying etiology.", "steps": ["Confirm the opacity is sharply branching tubular structures representing air-filled bronchi surrounded by consolidated alveoli).", "Differentiate based on internal pattern: Air bronchograms within a fissure-defined opacity strongly suggest alveolar filling (classically infectious pneumonia); absence of air bronchograms or presence of a mass-like density suggests neoplasm; bilateral perihilar distribution without fissure respect Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following observations best supports the diagnosis of pneumorrhachis in this patient, considering the clinical background provided?

A) Presence of extensive pneumomediastinum with air outlining the cardiac silhouette on Figure 1.
B) Visualization of air within the spinal canal on Figure 1, with air also seen in the right neural exit foramen on Figure 3.
C) Observation of a subtle left pneumothorax on Figure 2, with air in the oblique fissure.
D) Detection of subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and upper thorax on Figure 1, with air outlining the trachea.
E) Identification of pleural effusion on the left side on Figure 2, causing mediastinal shift.
F) Extensive air in the subcutaneous tissue of the chest wall on Figure 3, with no involvement of the spinal canal.
